the tuning of fractional-order controllers is possible and the use of fractional-order controllers can lead to improved control performance.

a new class of fractional-order PI and PI–D controllers can be defined, based on closed-loop reference models, and that a tuning method based upon the time moments approach can be proposed for more complex systems.
a new class of fractional-order proportional– integral–derivative (PI) controllers is defined based on a closed loop reference model expressing the dynamics and robustness performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a new class, of fractional-order PID (FOPID) controllers.
the development of new fractional-order control strategies for industrial applications.
the development of new fractional-order proportional–derivative controllers that are able to provide a better compromise between robustness and performance, and are easier to tune.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fractional PID controllers can be considered as a new class of controllers with improved performances, which are able to overcome the limitations of classical PID controllers.
fractional PID control can be a very effective tool in the design of robust control systems.
fractional-order PID controllers are very promising for the control of industrial systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tuning of a new class (fractional) of robust PID controllers is proposed, based on a new class of closed-loop reference models expressing the dynamical performance and robustness.
the tuning of fractional-order PID controllers is not a straightforward extension of the tuning of integer-order PID controllers.
the new class of fractional PID controllers is very promising for industrial applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fractional PID controllers can be tuned using a closed-loop reference-model approach, in a similar way as conventional PID controllers.
fractional-order controllers can be tuned in a systematic way, using the same principles as for integer-order controllers.
the fractional PID controllers, which are based on the fractional calculus, can be used to design robust controllers for a wide class of linear systems.
